content.user_title: Build Go Services with Uber Fx
content.value_statement: Complex Go services need predictable dependency wiring and lifecycle management. This skill provides practical Uber Fx guidance for modular applications, graceful shutdown, and focused tests.
actual_capabilities: Designs Fx composition roots with providers, invokes, modules, and annotations.
Moves server and worker startup into lifecycle hooks with graceful shutdown.
Models named dependencies, value groups, optional inputs, and interface bindings.
Uses Supply, Replace, Decorate, and Populate for configuration and tests.
Builds fxtest patterns for graph validation, dependency replacement, and lifecycle assertions.
Compares Uber Fx with raw Dig for lifecycle-free programs.
limitations: Provides guidance, but does not check current package versions or vulnerability databases without external tools.
Does not compile or test generated Go code unless the host grants command access.
Assumes familiarity with Go constructors, interfaces, contexts, and basic dependency injection.
Examples require adaptation for each service, especially logging, error handling, and shutdown behavior.

use_cases.title: Migrate a Go service
use_cases.description: Restructure manual application wiring into Fx providers, invokes, modules, and lifecycle hooks.

use_cases.title: Standardize service modules
use_cases.description: Define reusable HTTP, database, metrics, and worker modules with clear ownership and scoped decorators.

use_cases.title: Test dependency graphs
use_cases.description: Validate production wiring and replace real dependencies with fakes through fxtest utilities.

prompt_templates.title: Wire a basic service
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain how to wire my Go service with Uber Fx. Use these constructors: [constructors]. Identify the required Provide and Invoke calls.

prompt_templates.title: Add lifecycle hooks
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor this startup flow into Fx lifecycle hooks: [current flow]. Keep OnStart nonblocking and implement graceful shutdown with context cancellation.

prompt_templates.title: Design modular wiring
prompt_templates.prompt: Design Fx modules for these service areas: [areas]. Show provider ownership, scoped decorators, named dependencies, and value groups where appropriate.

prompt_templates.title: Audit an Fx graph
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this Uber Fx composition root: [implementation]. Find missing providers, lifecycle hazards, annotation errors, unordered groups, and test gaps. Propose focused fixes.

output_examples.input: A server constructor starts listening immediately and blocks application startup.
output: Move listener creation and serving into an OnStart hook.
Start the blocking serve loop in a goroutine so OnStart returns promptly.
Register an OnStop hook that performs graceful shutdown with the provided context.

output_examples.input: HTTP, database, metrics, and worker providers are mixed in one composition root.
output: Create one Fx module for each service area.
Keep shared configuration and logging providers at the application root.
Place concern-specific providers, invokes, and decorators inside their owning modules.

output_examples.input: An integration test needs an erroring database without changing the production module.
output: Compose the existing production module in an fxtest application.
Replace the database interface with the erroring fake.
Populate the service under test, start the application, assert behavior, and stop it.

best_practices: Keep the composition root small and organize related providers inside named modules.
Put side effects in lifecycle hooks and honor cancellation during startup and shutdown.
Validate the production graph in tests and replace external dependencies with focused fakes.
anti_patterns: Do not start blocking work inside constructors or synchronous OnStart hooks.
Do not assume value groups preserve registration order.
Do not hide required infrastructure behind optional dependencies.

faq.question: When should I use Uber Fx?
faq.answer: Use Fx for long-running Go services that need dependency wiring, lifecycle hooks, signal handling, and modular composition.

faq.question: When is raw Dig a better choice?
faq.answer: Use Dig when you need dependency injection without application lifecycle management, especially in libraries or small command-line tools.

faq.question: Does the skill run my application?
faq.answer: No. It provides implementation guidance and only runs tools when the host grants access and the user requests execution.

faq.question: Can it help with graceful shutdown?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains OnStart and OnStop hooks, timeout contexts, signal handling, and orderly resource cleanup.

faq.question: Can it help test an Fx application?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers fxtest, Populate, Replace, standalone lifecycle tests, event capture, and production graph validation.

faq.question: Does it choose application-specific dependencies?
faq.answer: No. You must provide your constructors, interfaces, configuration requirements, and operational constraints.
